newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 21.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 21.6 percent.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said on Friday program trading averaged 21.6 percent of its average daily volume of 529.5 million shares, or 114.4 million shares a day, during the week of December 16-20.
Buy programs accounted for a daily average of 68.1 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average of 46.3 million shares, the exchange said.
In all markets, program trading during the week of December 16-20 averaged 175.6 million shares a day.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, Salomon Brothers, BNP Securities and Susquehanna Brokerage Services executed most of their program activity for customers. Morgan Stanley executed most of its program trading as principal. Lehman Brothers split its program activity between its own account and those of customers.
During that week 22.7 percent of program volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage and another 8.2 percent involved derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses portfolio trading strategies involving the purchase or sale of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a total value of $1 million or more.
